title: brew cleanup not freeing space on Mac (Homebrew cache fix)
short_title: brew cleanup frees almost nothing? Clear the Homebrew cache

runs.output: ==> This operation would free approximately 22.9MB of disk space.
==> This operation would free approximately 780.6MB of disk space.

verify.notes: Homebrew 7.0.9 on Ben's Mac, 2026-10-17. Only dry runs were executed; nothing was removed. The manpage says plain cleanup removes downloads more than 120 days old (HOMEBREW_CLEANUP_MAX_AGE_DAYS) and --prune=all removes every cache file. 723M of the 789M cache is the downloads folder.

scenes.title: brew cleanup frees almost nothing
scenes.narration: If you run brew cleanup on a Mac and it frees almost nothing, while the Homebrew cache is still hundreds of megabytes, here is why, and how to clear it.

scenes.label: Terminal
lines: ==> This operation would free approximately 22.9MB of disk space.
scenes.narration: On this Mac the Homebrew cache holds 789 megabytes. A preview of a plain brew cleanup says it would free about 23 of them.

scenes.text: Plain brew cleanup only removes downloads more than 120 days old.
scenes.narration: By default, brew cleanup only removes downloads that are more than 120 days old. Everything you installed or upgraded recently stays in the cache.

scenes.label: Terminal
scenes.ui: Installed packages stay installed. A reinstall downloads its files again.
scenes.narration: Add prune equals all. Run it with dry run first to see the list, then run it again without dry run. Your installed packages stay installed; a reinstall simply downloads its files again.

scenes.label: Terminal
lines: ==> This operation would free approximately 780.6MB of disk space.
scenes.narration: Here the preview with prune all says it would free about 780 megabytes, nearly the whole cache, instead of 23.

scenes.name: Legroom
scenes.line: Knows the Homebrew downloads cache. Shows a preview, and cleans only what you approve.
scenes.narration: Legroom is a menu bar app for Mac disk space. It knows caches such as Homebrew downloads, Xcode DerivedData and the npm cache. A rule shows a preview of exactly what it would remove, and nothing goes until you approve it. It can run on a schedule, or when free space drops below a line you set. There is a free seven day trial.
